characters: Adwoa: an eight-year-old Ghanaian girl with neat braided puffs and red hair beads, wearing a bright coral-orange dress and brown sandals, carrying a woven market basket.
Mama: Adwoa’s warm mother wearing a blue-and-yellow wax-print wrapper and headscarf.
Auntie Dede: a busy, friendly market vegetable seller wearing a red-and-gold head-tie and cloth apron.

narrationPlan.pace: Slow-medium (about 105 words per minute) so children can do the mental sums along with Adwoa.
notes: Pause briefly after each sum so young listeners can calculate along.

music: Optional low-key soft piano ambience (user-togglable in reader header; off by default).
culturalNotes: Uses authentic Ghanaian currency (cedis) and market items (kontomire, tomatoes, salt).

pages.brief: Sunny Ghanaian home courtyard: Mama (blue-and-yellow wax-print dress) handing a twenty-cedi note and woven basket to eight-year-old Adwoa (braided puffs with red beads, coral-orange dress).
pages.narration: Warm and encouraging. Emphasise "twenty-cedi note" and "Count the prices and your change carefully".

pages.brief: At Auntie Dede’s colourful vegetable stall, Adwoa holds three fresh green bunches of kontomire leaves and counts on her fingers while Auntie Dede smiles.
pages.narration: Clear, rhythmic counting: "Two, four, six. Three bunches cost six cedis."

pages.brief: Auntie Dede pouring shiny red tomatoes from a small measure bowl into Adwoa’s woven basket; Adwoa thinking carefully.
pages.narration: Slow and clear on the addition: "Six cedis... plus five cedis... makes eleven cedis."

pages.brief: Close view of Adwoa placing a neat white packet of salt (no text) into her woven basket beside the green kontomire leaves and red tomatoes.
Adwoa holding out her twenty-cedi note at the busy stall while two other market shoppers wait beside Auntie Dede.
pages.narration: Quiet and confident as Adwoa works out the subtraction.

pages.brief: Busy market scene: Auntie Dede turning toward waiting shoppers while pressing two banknotes into Adwoa’s hand.
Under the dappled shade of a neem tree at the market edge, Adwoa stops with her basket and looks closely at the two banknotes in her open palm.
pages.narration: Surprised discovery, then slow, clear arithmetic: "Five cedis plus five cedis was ten cedis... Ten minus six is four."

pages.brief: Adwoa walking past a mango stall with a determined, honest expression, heading straight back toward Auntie Dede’s vegetable stall.
pages.narration: Brief pause on the temptation of the mangoes, then warm resolve.

pages.brief: At the vegetable stall, Auntie Dede smiles gratefully with her hand on her heart, handing Adwoa one banknote and one coin while Adwoa beams proudly.
pages.narration: Warm, joyful, and proud. Slow down on the final sentence and pause before "The end".

teacherGuide.overview: A Primary 2–3 mathematics and character story set in a Ghanaian market. Learners practise multiplication by 2, multi-step addition within 20, subtraction to find change from 20 cedis, and the value of honesty when an error occurs.
learningGoals: Calculate the total cost of multiple items using skip-counting and addition within 20 cedis.
Find the correct change from a 20-cedi note by subtracting or counting up.
Identify a calculation discrepancy (10 − 6 = 4 cedis) and explain why returning extra change is honest.

subjectLinks.subject: Religious and Moral Education / Our World Our People

beforeReading: Show learners paper play-money (1, 2, 5, 10 and 20 cedi notes/coins) and practise making 6 cedis and 14 cedis.
whileReading: Pause after page 4 and let every child check Adwoa’s total: 6 + 5 + 3 = 14 cedis.
Pause after page 7 and ask how Adwoa knew she had 4 cedis too much.
afterReading: Set up a classroom market corner where pairs take turns being the buyer (with 20 cedis) and the shopkeeper checking the change together.
discussion: How did doing the maths in her head before paying help Adwoa notice the mistake?
Why was it tempting to keep the four cedis, and what helped Adwoa choose honesty?
reflection: Have you ever found something or received extra change that was not yours? What did you do?

mathsExtension.task: 3 bunches of kontomire at 2 cedis each = ?
Change from 20 cedis when spending 14 cedis = ?
Difference between 10 cedis received and 6 cedis correct change = ?

support: Use 20 counters on a ten-frame mat to remove 6, 5, and 3 counters physically and count the 6 left.
stretch: What if Adwoa also bought 2 onions at 1 cedi each? Recalculate the total (16 cedis) and change from 20 cedis (4 cedis).

culturalNotes: Adwoa is an Akan day name for a girl born on Monday.
Kontomire (cocoyam leaves) is a staple leafy green used across Ghana for stews and palava sauce.
localiseThis: Adjust market item names to the everyday greens and vegetables sold in your town.

pronunciation.guidance: "ah-JWAH". The "dw" is the hard part for English engines and is probably not a plain "d" + "w".
reviewerNotes: HIGH RISK: the "dw" cluster. Native speaker to demonstrate and approve a rendering.
Confirm language of origin and meaning before it appears in teacher notes.
